title: Bijectivity of normalized torsor section evaluation
statement: With $V,\ell,P,c:Y\to V,F,A$ as in the fixed connected torsor setting, suppose $c^*F\cong\underline A_Y$ [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $N_F,Q_F$ be the canonical section representation and equivariant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsor-section-representation]. For any supplied natural module morphism $\alpha:F\to Q_F$ normalized by $\alpha_Y(s)(\Delta(y))=s$ for every $s\in F(Y)$ and $y\in Y$, the component $\alpha_W:F(W)\to Q_F(W)$ is bijective for every etale object $W$ of $V$. No finite generation is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0DV5 (3), 0DV6 and 0A3R, proof identifying the restricted representation; sites.tex Tags 04TR and 04TS (gluing sheaves and mapping property), with module operations as in 0DV5 (3); explicit section-evaluation implementation of the fixed-torsor argument

proof.text: The constant pullback and connectedness identify the restriction of F to Y with the locally constant function sheaf of value F(Y). Every section over T etale over Y is locally a restriction of some x in F(Y). Naturality of alpha along T to Y and its diagonal normalization determine its value on the graph of T to Y. Torsor equivariance determines all other values, because the translates of that graph exhaust T times_V Y. Hence alpha locally is the canonical evaluation map.

If alpha_W(s)=0, the local evaluation formula shows that s restricts to zero over W times_V Y. This is an etale surjective cover of W, so the sheaf separatedness of F gives s=0. By linearity this proves injectivity.

An equivariant locally constant function on W times_V Y is a section of the restriction of F. On its double overlap the torsor isomorphism gives components indexed by P. On the component g, agreement of the two restrictions is precisely t(g y)=F(g inverse)(t(y)). The sheaf gluing axiom therefore descends the section to W. The local evaluation formula shows that its image under alpha is the original function. This proves surjectivity, including the empty W and zero-module cases.

theorem Scheme.GaloisCover.sectionEvaluation_bijective
    {V : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace V] (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (P : Type u) [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) V) [ConnectedSpace c.P]
    (F : Sheaf V.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))))
    (A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))
    (h : Nonempty ((c.π)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ))].obj F ≅
      (constantSheaf c.P.smallEtaleTopology
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))).obj A))
    (α : F.obj ⟶ c.sectionRepresentationPresheaf ℓ F)
    (hα : c.SectionEvaluationNormalized ℓ F α) (W : V.Etaleᵒᵖ) :
    Function.Bijective (α.app W)
